solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To offer no resistance is good behaviour

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the verb in the grid

parts.note: super is an informal word for very good
conduct is the way someone behaves

explanation.surface: A moral maxim: meek compliance, never pushing back, counts as good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' reads as moral opposition but the definition is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A superconductor carries electric current with zero electrical resistance, so to superconduct is to let current pass unopposed.

clue.text: Remove ring of dirt, really showing pale lustre

indicators.note: an instruction to take something out of the word that follows

parts.note: soil is earth or dirt
a ring is round, like the letter O
very and really are both intensifiers

explanation.surface: Cleaning advice: scrub off the ring of grime and the item gleams with a soft sheen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that shines with a pale, soft gleam is described as silver-like in colour and sheen.

clue.text: Not a lot to be said that's comforting

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the word for not a lot is heard rather than written

parts.note: few means not many, not a lot

explanation.surface: A minimalist's line about reassurance: only a few words are needed to comfort someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of relief is what you say when something reassuring happens, a sigh that the danger has passed.

clue.text: Maigret readership includes one brought out of retirement

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer's letters within them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: Simenon's detective is so popular that his readers include a pensioner tempted back.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is informally a person recalled to work after retiring, from a tyre given new tread.

clue.text: Supposedly wise to have outstanding guards slay uprising

indicators.note: the outer piece stands around the inner one, protecting it

parts.note: to owe is to have a debt still outstanding

indicators.note: in a down clue the word rises, so it is written bottom to top

parts.note: slay means kill

explanation.surface: A fable-like scene: being wise means having sentries guard against a rising rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' tempts as 'excellent', but 'to have outstanding' means to be in debt. 'uprising' reverses KILL to LLIK.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is traditionally a symbol of wisdom, so resembling one implies a reputation for being wise.

clue.text: Republican eliminated in tense beginning

indicators.note: the letter is knocked out of the word

parts.note: a drawn face is tense and strained

explanation.surface: A political thriller: a Republican is knocked out at the start of a nervy contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the first light of day and, figuratively, the start of anything.

clue.text: Lombardy town where romance stirs?

indicators.note: stirring mixes things, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A travel question: in which northern Italian town is love in the air?
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, famed for Stradivarius violins.

clue.text: Setting up English, try hard workers in roster

parts.note: to have a stab is to have a try

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the following word

parts.note: a roster is a list of duty names
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A manager setting up a team: try putting the hard workers on the English rota.
explanation.definitionFit: Establishment is the act of founding or setting something up, as of a company.

clue.text: Foes may be reconciled by one bluebird flying around hilltop

definitions.text: Foes may be reconciled by one

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the other piece
a bird in flight is all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ridge is the crest along the top of a hill

explanation.surface: A peace-dove image: a bluebird circling a hill brings old enemies together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' makes BBUILDER, the anagram; 'around' wraps it about the hilltop. The surface bird of peace hints at the reconciling definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who builds bridges in the figurative sense works to reconcile opposing parties.

clue.text: Signal was positioned about right for property

definitions.note: used as an adjective meaning striking or notable

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: sat means was placed or situated
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Estate-agent jargon: a signpost stood beside a right of way over a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' looks like a noun but is the adjective, as in 'a signal success'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something prominent and conspicuous, standing out from its surroundings.

clue.text: Cattle sound effects that may be useful when driving uphill

definitions.text: that may be useful when driving uphill

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make
gear means personal belongings or effects

explanation.surface: A sound engineer's catalogue: mooing noises are handy for a rural driving scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound effects' reads as one unit but splits: cattle sound, then effects.
explanation.definitionFit: A low gear gives more pulling power at low speed, which a car needs on a steep climb.

clue.text: Chicago's cut its rail service for spring (on ice)

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of the verb meaning to cut, as written in Chicago
the El is Chicago's elevated railway; 'its' refers back to the city

explanation.surface: A local news item: the city has slashed funding for its trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicago's' does double duty in the surface but in the wordplay asks for the American spelling AX; the El is the city's elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a figure-skating jump, a leap made on the ice.

clue.text: Usual food with soft filling knocked back without enthusiasm

indicators.note: something knocked back goes backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the letter goes inside, as a filling

parts.note: your diet is what you usually eat
P, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A diner unimpressed by a regular meal with a soft centre, gulped down half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' makes DIPET; 'knocked back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lukewarm response is a half-hearted one, so this temperature word also means lacking enthusiasm.

clue.text: Fine antique pen

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
antique means old

explanation.surface: A collector's description of a fine old writing instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is not a writing implement but an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold is an enclosure for sheep, just as a pen is.

clue.text: Gradually destroy upright, half-forgotten Dumbledore

indicators.note: in a down clue standing upright means read from the bottom up
the first half of the name is dropped, leaving the last five letters

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter fan's lament: the headmaster stands tall but half his story is forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-forgotten' leaves EDORE; 'upright' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away gradually, as water does rock, is to destroy something slowly.

clue.text: 'Apple-brandy' bargain that can't be bettered?

parts.note: i is the Apple brand prefix, as in iPhone and iPad, so 'Apple-brandy' means like an Apple brand name
a deal is a bargain

explanation.surface: A shopper raves about a deal on calvados, the perfect bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple-brandy' looks like calvados but is a jokey adjective: Apple products carry the small i prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect is by definition the best possible, beyond improvement.

clue.text: Labour's leader indeed socialist on more than one level?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: aye is an emphatic yes, indeed
red is a familiar term for a socialist

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the Labour leader is truly socialist, and on several levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged in layers sits on several levels, one above another.

clue.text: Aged men contrived last moves

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly men staging a final scheme, perhaps at the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final stage of a chess game, the last series of moves.

clue.text: Lake becoming river in long and thin turn for water extraction

indicators.note: one letter turns into another

parts.note: spindly means long, thin and weak

explanation.surface: Geography of a lake that narrows into a long, thin river after a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is not a bend in water but a spin of a washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin cycle whirls laundry fast to throw the water out, a turning to extract moisture.

clue.text: Gather round my people: I'll help to make tea

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to gather is to infer or conclude
us is the speaker's own group, my people

explanation.surface: A host calling everyone together and offering to brew up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer device that holds leaves while they steep, helping the tea brew.

clue.text: Great flower in manly nature article, unknown for its heart

parts.note: in Chinese philosophy yang is the masculine principle

indicators.note: the middle letter is replaced

parts.note: the is the definite article
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A lifestyle piece praising a magnificent bloom as masculine, its centre a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (something that flows). In THE, H gives way to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of China, the longest in Asia, flows to the sea at Shanghai.

clue.text: Gold on trophy table

indicators.note: in an across clue the gold comes after the trophy

parts.note: a plate is a trophy for a race, as in a cup or plate
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Prize-giving: a golden trophy laid on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' means tableland, flat high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high level ground, also called a tableland.

clue.text: Condition extra-large Welsh engine with power raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means reading upwards

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, extra-large clothing
Ivor the Engine is the steam engine of a British children's TV series set in Wales
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A railway enthusiast's job: a big Welsh locomotive with its power boosted.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor the Engine was a British animated series about a little Welsh railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation attached to an agreement.

clue.text: The same European experiencing many a storm front leaves

indicators.note: the front letter of the word goes away

parts.note: squally weather has frequent sudden storms

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that each storm front strips the leaves from trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' suggests a weather front, but here it is the first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means in the same way or to the same degree.

clue.text: Millitary intelligence folios are infuriating

definitions.note: a plural verb phrase fitting the plural subject of the clue; the answer is the verb to annoy

parts.note: MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5
ff is the abbreviation for folios

explanation.surface: Office grumble: secret-service files drive everyone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To miff is to irritate or offend someone, a mild form of making them angry.

clue.text: Perhaps to enter managed bar?

parts.note: in is the word for entry, as in 'come in'
got means managed, as in 'got there'

explanation.surface: A question about a pub: did someone manage to get in to a run bar?
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed bar' reads as a pub, but 'managed to enter' is GOT IN, here written as IN + GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically gold, in the form of a bar.

clue.text: No gentleman left to turn up

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, the opposite of a gentleman

explanation.surface: An etiquette complaint: no gentleman remained to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' suggests arriving, but means to twist upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl is to bend or twist upward, as hair or a lip does.

clue.text: One year for Cocteau to make his name?

parts.note: in French the first person 'I', one, is je; Cocteau's French governs both words
Cocteau was French, and the French for year is an

explanation.surface: The French poet chooses a year to establish himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Cocteau was a French writer and film-maker, so 'for Cocteau' asks for French words.
explanation.definitionFit: The French artist's first name, which completes his full name with the surname given.

clue.text: Notice jam stain

definitions.meaning: a tight ... is a jam or predicament

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's note about jam marks on a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the three words is a common meaning of the same short word: to see, a tight fix, a mark.

clue.text: Sides of Nazca trail emerging

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by a hound

explanation.surface: Archaeology: the edges of a Nazca line becoming visible in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nazca lines are huge ancient figures in the Peruvian desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence and beginning to develop.

clue.text: Terror exploit covering Liberal motivation?

parts.note: a little terror is a mischievous child, an imp

indicators.note: the outer word wraps around the letter

parts.note: to use is to exploit

explanation.surface: A political thriller: an act of terror covering for a Liberal's motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terror' reads as violence but means a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge that drives action, a kind of motivation.

clue.text: Excruciating wry hectoring is out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rebuke: sarcastic bullying is unacceptable and painful to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something embarrassing enough to make you wince is painfully awkward.
